applies_why: The judge text decides a link by noting the chapter-bound witnesses are real but a concession and word-count leave it underdetermined, so it is the kind of chain-level collision K-C governs.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse' could mean the judge must expressly compare whole chains rather than list individual verse points; the text treats the chapter bounds as a set and also notes a concession and a lexical point, which is not clearly a prohibited verse-by-verse stating-verse test.
why: The judge acknowledges the chapter-bound chain as real and decides underdetermined based on a concession and a two-way word-count, rather than dismissing the chain because no single verse states the contrary.
